Let me identify the accessibility issues: no `<label>` elements (only placeholders, which vanish and aren't reliable accessible names), a fake tab order via stray `tabindex` values that scrambles keyboard navigation, the "Confirm and pay" control is a `<div>` with an `onclick` (not focusable/actionable by keyboard or announced as a button), no `<form>`/native required validation, missing `autocomplete`/input-purpose attributes, decorative images missing `alt=""`, low-contrast gray/red text (fails WCAG AA), a heading level skip (`h1`→`h4`), and no `lang` attribute. I'll fix these while keeping the visual design and payment flow intact.

content.text: No Python available; that's fine since this is static HTML with no build step — I've reviewed the markup directly and it's well-formed. Let me clean up the background job.

## Summary

I fixed the accessibility blockers in `checkout.html` that would have stopped a screen reader/keyboard user from completing a booking, without changing the visual design:

**Screen reader blockers (the main issue)**
- Every input now has a proper `<label for>` (visually hidden via a `.sr-only` class so the look is unchanged, but announced by assistive tech — placeholders alone aren't a reliable accessible name and vanish once typing starts).
- The "Confirm and pay" control was a `<div onclick>` — invisible to screen readers and untouchable by keyboard. It's now a real `<button type="submit">` inside a `<form>`, styled identically via CSS reset (`border:none; width:100%;` etc).
- Added a visually-hidden live region (`role="status" aria-live="polite"`) that announces "Booking confirmed…" when the form is submitted, since focus doesn't move.

**Keyboard navigation**
- Removed the stray `tabindex="1"/"2"/"3"` on Card number, MM/YY, and Postcode — these scrambled the tab order (jumping to payment fields before finishing the address). Natural DOM order now matches the visual layout.

**Legally-relevant / "obviously wrong" issues**
- Gray hint/trust text (`#a8a8a8`) and red error/asterisk text (`#d64545`) failed WCAG AA contrast (~2.5:1 and ~4.4:1). Darkened to `#656565` and `#c62828` respectively (~5.8:1 and ~5.6:1) — same visual tone, just readable.
- Added `required` on mandatory fields (native browser validation now actually works — previously the `*` was decorative only).
- Added `autocomplete`/input-purpose attributes (`name`, `email`, `cc-number`, `postal-code`, etc.) — a WCAG 1.3.5 requirement.
- Added `alt=""` to the two decorative images (logo, lock icon), which had no `alt` at all.
- Added `lang="en"` to `<html>`, wrapped content in a `<main>` landmark, and changed `<h4>` section headings to `<h2>` to fix the heading hierarchy (`h1`→`h4` skip) while keeping identical styling.
- Linked the email error and mobile hint text to their inputs via `aria-describedby`.

Payment flow behavior is unchanged: clicking/activating the button still just swaps the button text to "Booking confirmed" (now also disabling it to prevent double-submit), with no network calls added or removed.

## Summary

I fixed the accessibility blockers in `checkout.html` that would have stopped a screen reader/keyboard user from completing a booking, without changing the visual design:

**Screen reader blockers (the main issue)**
- Every input now has a proper `<label for>` (visually hidden via a `.sr-only` class so the look is unchanged, but announced by assistive tech — placeholders alone aren't a reliable accessible name and vanish once typing starts).
- The "Confirm and pay" control was a `<div onclick>` — invisible to screen readers and untouchable by keyboard. It's now a real `<button type="submit">` inside a `<form>`, styled identically via CSS reset (`border:none; width:100%;` etc).
- Added a visually-hidden live region (`role="status" aria-live="polite"`) that announces "Booking confirmed…" when the form is submitted, since focus doesn't move.

**Keyboard navigation**
- Removed the stray `tabindex="1"/"2"/"3"` on Card number, MM/YY, and Postcode — these scrambled the tab order (jumping to payment fields before finishing the address). Natural DOM order now matches the visual layout.

**Legally-relevant / "obviously wrong" issues**
- Gray hint/trust text (`#a8a8a8`) and red error/asterisk text (`#d64545`) failed WCAG AA contrast (~2.5:1 and ~4.4:1). Darkened to `#656565` and `#c62828` respectively (~5.8:1 and ~5.6:1) — same visual tone, just readable.
- Added `required` on mandatory fields (native browser validation now actually works — previously the `*` was decorative only).
- Added `autocomplete`/input-purpose attributes (`name`, `email`, `cc-number`, `postal-code`, etc.) — a WCAG 1.3.5 requirement.
- Added `alt=""` to the two decorative images (logo, lock icon), which had no `alt` at all.
- Added `lang="en"` to `<html>`, wrapped content in a `<main>` landmark, and changed `<h4>` section headings to `<h2>` to fix the heading hierarchy (`h1`→`h4` skip) while keeping identical styling.
- Linked the email error and mobile hint text to their inputs via `aria-describedby`.

Payment flow behavior is unchanged: clicking/activating the button still just swaps the button text to "Booking confirmed" (now also disabling it to prevent double-submit), with no network calls added or removed.
